title: The Star That's Older Than The Universe
description:
For years, one star's age estimate was older than the universe it lives in. It's not magic, it's measurement error — but the story shows how astronomers actually date the cosmos.

#shorts #sciencefacts #space

scenes.text: There is a star that, for a while, was calculated to be older than the universe itself.
It's called HD 140283, nicknamed the Methuselah star, and it sits about two hundred light years away.
Early measurements put its age at around sixteen billion years. The universe itself is only about thirteen point eight billion years old.
That's a paradox. A star cannot be older than the universe that made it.
The fix came from the Hubble Space Telescope, which narrowed the star's age to around fourteen point five billion years, with enough uncertainty to fit inside the universe's real age after all.
Still one of the oldest stars ever found, and a reminder that even the universe's age comes with error bars.
